Passage A16 - What Changes When the Ground Gets Harder

Putting a number on each surface (drop test: a basketball released from two metres, rebound height recorded)
- the coefficient of restitution rises as a surface gives back more of the energy delivered to it
- artificial grass, which gave back the least: (4) ........
- synthetic rubber: 0.320
- concrete, the hardest of the three: (5) ........

In the laboratory
- runway fifteen metres long and one metre wide; ten cameras, plus a force plate set flush into the floor at the midpoint
- runners crossed at (6) ........ metres per second, a run counting only if the measured speed stayed within 0.2 of that figure and the whole foot landed on the plate
- five clean runs collected from every runner on every surface

Passage A18 - Naming a Species from a Short Piece of DNA

Building one entry for the library
- Step 1: take a specimen an expert has already named, usually out of a (7) ........ , and write down where and when it was caught
- Step 2: remove a single leg as the tissue sample, so that the rest of the animal survives as a (8) ........ and can be examined again later
- Step 3: copy the gene fragment in a machine that runs (9) ........ rounds of heating and cooling
- Step 4: read the sequence of the copy
- Step 5: upload the sequence to a shared online database, beside a photograph of the specimen and its collection record

Three routes to a name (share of species correctly named)
- barcodes alone: 89.9 per cent
- appearance alone: females 89.7 per cent, males (10) ........ per cent
- the two used together: females 96.3 per cent, males (11) ........ per cent
- of eight pairs that are notoriously hard to tell apart by eye, (12) ........ were divided cleanly by their barcodes

Passage A19 - Turning Salt Water into Drinking Water with Sunlight

What the trials produced (readings taken every hour from 08:00 to 17:00)
